[[File:Kyle Heuer DecipherCon 2002.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Kyle Heuer at DecipherCon 2002.]]
'''Kyle Heuer''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Red 7 from Decipher Inc.; Rogue Leader from Decipher Inc.. The published fan table records status: Now Rogue Leader.

== Squadron listing ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Slot !! Town !! Status (fan table)
|-
| Red 7 || Decipher Inc. || Now Rogue Leader
|-
| Rogue Leader || Decipher Inc. || Retired
|}

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Anagrams ==

A GeoCities fan page (copied onto Encyclopedia 3.2 p.200) maps these printed titles:

* [[Elyhek Rue]] — Kyle Heuer, Rogue Leader

== Other sourced notes ==

Listed as Red 7 (Decipher Inc.), later Rogue Leader. After RFD episode 30 he and Evan Lorentz took over regular hosting from Carol Wisely.

The anagram list unscrambles [[Elyhek Rue]] as Kyle Heuer.

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Heuer is credited on Decipher's [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] team. As Product Champion Coordinator he led the Product Champions' promotion of the game and was its video reporter.<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="jkpersonae">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/designdiary/personae.html Design Diary: Dramatis personae], decipher.com (2000–2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010224092942/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/designdiary/personae.html Internet Archive]</ref>
